messages:
amy: Quick heads-up — planning a rolling maintenance window for the meridian-gpu-pool (eu-central) next Tue 02:00-08:00 UTC. Purpose: NIC microcode + driver hotpatch.
amy: Plan is cohorted reboots: 10 racks, 6 cohorts, ~30m cordon/drain + 20m reboot + 10m uncordon per cohort. We'll keep one spare rack as backfill.
amy: Expected customer impact: transient queueing and a small bump in latency for warmups; no planned 503s.
sanjay: Can we avoid hitting Dedicated reserved capacity guarantees? Which tenants are on meridian-pool?
amy: We're excluding priority-tenants. Reserved/Dedicated customers will be routed to eu-backup-pool via routing policy 'region-fallback' during each cohort.
marta: Please add a KV/prefix-cache seed step before each cohort uncordon to avoid cold-token costs. If we don't, embedding/llm synth loads spike and cost goes up.
lee: Agree. Suggest: run prefix cache seed + a quick perf probe job (100 short-gen calls) 5m after uncordon. If latencies > 300ms we pause canary.
amy: Good. I'll add that to the runbook. Here's the drain snippet I'll use:
```
kubectl cordon <node>
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --pod-selector='app!=infra-agent' --grace-period=120
```
amy: We'll run the above in parallel up to 4 nodes per cohort to avoid backpressure on scheduler.
sanjay: Networking note: NIC firmware patch has a short window where link flaps are possible for ~30s after reboot. We should stagger reboots inside each rack by ~90s to avoid simultaneous egress dips.
amy: Staggering + backfill strategy noted.
ops-oncall: infra-bot will create the incident/maintenance ticket and page if any dataplane alerts cross threshold during the window. Alert thresholds: p90>350ms OR 5% error increase.
infra-bot: Maintenance created — ID MI-2026-0423, scheduled Tue 02:00-08:00 UTC, cohorts created: 6. Webhook: https://internal.redwood/maint/MI-2026-0423
marta: Cost tradeoff — prewarmed KV cache run will add ~0.6M token ops across the pool (est). That's cheaper than cold-started token churn if we avoid regen. Approve?
sanjay: Approve. Also add a step to temporarily lower batch size for 15m after each cohort to reduce latency tail while caches reseed.
amy: Will do. Add to runbook: prewarm -> probe -> lower-batch -> monitor 20m -> restore batch size.
lee: Can we run a canary cohort first on a single rack during low traffic? Prefer starting with cohort-6 (lowest priority).
amy: Yes. Canary scheduled at 02:00-02:30 UTC on rack-22. If metrics stable for 15m, proceed.
ops-oncall: Please post a short customer comms blurb to #announcements 24h prior and include expected 10-20m window per tenant at time of their routed switch.
amy: I'll draft the blurb. Draft: "Planned maintenance in eu-central Tue 02:00-08:00 UTC. Minimal impact expected; some requests may route to backup pools briefly. No action required."
marta: Also add runbook check: ensure KV seed job uses the same model variants as served (quantized vs fp16) to avoid quality regressions.
amy: Good catch. Added.
sanjay: After maintenance, run overnight synthetic load to validate perf and cost delta; capture tokens consumed and p95/p99 latencies.
lee: I'll own the synthetic job and dashboard refresh.
ops-oncall: Tagging oncall: @ops-oncall — standby for possible page.
amy: Thanks all — I'll post final schedule + runbook link in this thread once infra-bot creates the Jira and runbook page.
